purpose: Visual audit of 5 representative cycling events to determine whether ActivityClassifier cycling label is genuine or over-triggered
note: Frame numbers are extracted-frame indices (frame_skip=5). Frames inspected are before/event/after (frame_ref-1, frame_ref, frame_ref+1).

audited_tracks.visual_justification: Title card animation: 'When YOU are a Pedestrian'. All three frames show the film's animated title screen — a graphic silhouette of a traffic officer and animated child figures. No real person, no bicycle. YOLO detected silhouetted animated figures as persons. Signal 2 velocity over-trigger on animated title card graphics.

Indoor hospital scene. A doctor and nurse attend to a patient lying in a bed. The nurse is leaning over the patient and making arm movements across the patient's body. High mean_speed (0.507) is caused by the nurse's arm movement across the frame — not locomotion at all. No bicycle present. Indoors. Signal 2 firing on arm-motion velocity.

Outdoor pedestrian scene. A single man in a long overcoat is walking on a sidewalk beside a building. Upright walking posture, both feet visible, no bicycle. Three consecutive frames show him taking walking steps across the frame. No bicycle present. This is a pedestrian classified as cycling by Signal 2 (walking pace exceeded 0.018 threshold at 320x240 resolution).

Outdoor street intersection. Multiple pedestrians in overcoats and hats crossing a city street. A tram/bus is visible upper left. All subjects are clearly walking upright on foot. No bicycle or cyclist visible anywhere in frame. This is a classic pedestrian crossing scene. Signal 2 firing on walking-pace horizontal movement.

Outdoor residential/suburban street scene. Multiple children and one adult near a 1940s automobile parked at a crosswalk. Children are running or walking — one child in foreground appears to be jogging. No bicycle or cyclist anywhere in the three-frame sequence. Signal 2 triggered on children's movement pattern near a vehicle. This is a pedestrian safety demonstration scene.

decision_rationale: All 5 sampled cycling events are NOT_CYCLING. The subjects are: animated title card, medical staff making arm movements, a man walking on sidewalk, pedestrians crossing a street, children near a car. No bicycle appears in any of the 15 inspected frames. This is conclusive evidence that ActivityClassifier Signal 2 (velocity + height stability) is over-triggering severely at 320x240 resolution with frame_skip=5. The 0.018 normalized/s threshold is too low for this footage configuration.
root_cause_confirmed: CYCLE_HORIZ_THRESHOLD = 0.018 calibrated for 848px indoor footage fires on any movement >= ~1px/frame at 320x240. Stable bbox height (height_std < 0.03) is met by nearly all small/distant detection boxes. The combination causes near-universal misclassification of pedestrians as cyclists.
caveat: 5 samples are insufficient to claim a precise false-positive rate across the full 300s run. However 5/5 NOT_CYCLING from a distributed sample across 300s is strong evidence of systematic over-triggering.
